Work context｜O*NET 51-4022.00 work context shows: the work centers on equipment operation and setup and inspection and die maintenance, with noise, high temperature, heavy objects, and mechanical pinch points as the main environmental features.
Protection and noise｜Wearing common protective and safety equipment every day (99%), exposure to distracting noise every day (75%).

Posture and motion｜Continuous or almost continuous standing (86%), continuous use of hands to handle, control, or feel objects and tools (89%), and repetitive motions are common.
Communication and contact｜Face-to-face discussions with individuals and teams every day (87%), continuous contact with others (48%).
Pace and autonomy｜Work pace being determined by equipment speed being extremely important (38%), very little freedom to determine tasks and priorities (26%), fairly great decision-making freedom (46%).

Time and workload｜Time pressure every day (54%), a typical work week of more than 40 hours (54%).
Precision and consequences｜Precision or accuracy being important (36%), consequences of error being extremely serious (27%).
Responsibility and impact｜Very high responsibility for the health and safety of others (23%), decisions having an important impact on the results of coworkers and the unit (49%).

Environment and proximity｜Exposure to contaminants monthly but not weekly (34%), indoors in an uncontrolled environment, physical proximity being slightly close (12%).

Environment and pace｜Equipment, die setting, first-article, dimensional, and die maintenance tasks can coexist; the context option proportions do not represent everyone, and standing and noise proportions cannot be used to infer "medium-high" physical effort or daily high temperature. Actual shifts, lifting, equipment environment, and training should be checked with the employer.

Tools and materials｜The official tasks list forging equipment, dies and fixtures, hoisting equipment, hand tools, and dimensional measurement; check effective drawings and work orders, specified tolerances, and setup and maintenance procedures against the actual equipment. facts.display_value:
Occupational definition｜O*NET-SOC51-4022.00 sets up, operates, or tends forging machines to shape metal or plastic parts; tasks include reading the specified tolerances and process steps on work orders and drawings, setting and adjusting dies and fixtures, running and observing a first article, measuring dimensions, trimming and compressing forgings, and using hoisting equipment to install and remove dies and to repair or replace die parts. The official description also lists maintaining and repairing production tools, so maintenance and repair or in-process inspection cannot be excluded as a whole; complex electrical repair, design changes, and final
release authority must be checked against the specific position, equipment, and effective procedures and are not decided uniformly by the title.
